"""IBAN (International Bank Account Number) detector.

Validates the ISO 7064 MOD 97-10 checksum and the fixed length registered
for each country in the IBAN registry (SWIFT/ISO 13616). Both checks must
pass, which makes false positives rare: a random alphanumeric string of the
right shape has roughly a 1-in-97 chance of passing the checksum.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import re

from veil.types import Entity, EntityType, Span

# Registered IBAN length per country, from the IBAN registry (release 96,
# Society for Worldwide Interbank Financial Telecommunication / ISO 13616).
_COUNTRY_LENGTHS: dict[str, int] = {
    "AD": 24, "AE": 23, "AL": 28, "AT": 20, "AZ": 28, "BA": 20, "BE": 16,
    "BG": 22, "BH": 22, "BR": 29, "BY": 28, "CH": 21, "CR": 22, "CY": 28,
    "CZ": 24, "DE": 22, "DK": 18, "DO": 28, "EE": 20, "EG": 29, "ES": 24,
    "FI": 18, "FO": 18, "FR": 27, "GB": 22, "GE": 22, "GI": 23, "GL": 18,
    "GR": 27, "GT": 28, "HR": 21, "HU": 28, "IE": 22, "IL": 23, "IQ": 23,
    "IS": 26, "IT": 27, "JO": 30, "KW": 30, "KZ": 20, "LB": 28, "LC": 32,
    "LI": 21, "LT": 20, "LU": 20, "LV": 21, "LY": 25, "MC": 27, "MD": 24,
    "ME": 22, "MK": 19, "MR": 27, "MT": 31, "MU": 30, "NL": 18, "NO": 15,
    "PK": 24, "PL": 28, "PS": 29, "PT": 25, "QA": 29, "RO": 24, "RS": 22,
    "SA": 24, "SC": 31, "SD": 18, "SE": 24, "SI": 19, "SK": 24, "SM": 27,
    "ST": 25, "SV": 28, "TL": 23, "TN": 24, "TR": 26, "UA": 29, "VA": 22,
    "VG": 24, "XK": 20,
}  # fmt: skip

# IBANs are conventionally printed in uppercase (ISO 13616); requiring
# uppercase here keeps ordinary lowercase prose words from being pulled
# into a trailing group (e.g. "... 0130 00 by" would otherwise swallow "by").
_CANDIDATE_RE = re.compile(r"\b[A-Z]{2}\d{2}(?:[ ]?[A-Z0-9]{1,4}){2,7}\b")


def _mod97_ok(compact: str) -> bool:
    rearranged = compact[4:] + compact[:4]
    digits = "".join(str(int(ch, 36)) for ch in rearranged)
    return int(digits) % 97 == 1


def is_valid_iban(candidate: str) -> bool:
    compact = candidate.replace(" ", "").upper()
    if not re.fullmatch(r"[A-Z]{2}\d{2}[A-Z0-9]+", compact):
        return False
    country = compact[:2]
    expected_len = _COUNTRY_LENGTHS.get(country)
    if expected_len is None or len(compact) != expected_len:
        return False
    return _mod97_ok(compact)


class IbanDetector:
    name = "iban"

    def find(self, text: str) -> list[Entity]:
        out: list[Entity] = []
        for m in _CANDIDATE_RE.finditer(text):
            if not is_valid_iban(m.group(0)):
                continue
            out.append(
                Entity(
                    type=EntityType.IBAN,
                    value=m.group(0),
                    span=Span(m.start(), m.end()),
                    detector=self.name,
                    confidence=0.99,
                )
            )
        return out
veil/detectors/ip.py:
"""IPv4 and IPv6 address detector.

Candidate spans are matched with a cheap regex, then handed to the stdlib
``ipaddress`` module for authoritative parsing — this avoids re-deriving
IPv6's many valid shorthand forms (``::``, embedded IPv4, zone IDs) by hand.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import ipaddress
import re

from veil._spans import SpanIndex
from veil.types import Entity, EntityType, Span

# Trailing lookahead: block a following word char (glued alphanumeric) and
# specifically "another dotted digit" (a 5th octet - not a valid IPv4, so
# this candidate is really a prefix of some other dotted-number sequence).
# A bare trailing "." that *isn't* followed by a digit (ordinary sentence
# punctuation, e.g. "...at 10.0.0.1.") is deliberately allowed through.
_IPV4_RE = re.compile(r"(?<![\w.])(?:\d{1,3}\.){3}\d{1,3}(?!\w)(?!\.\d)")
# Consume the whole literal before validation. A hex-only expression can accept
# the valid prefix "2001:db8::192" of "2001:db8::192.0.2.33", exposing the rest.
# Zone identifiers are opaque local names/indices; retain their spelling,
# including percent escapes in bracketed URI literals, without resolving them.
_IPV6_RE = re.compile(
    r"(?<![\w:%.])[0-9A-Fa-f]*:[0-9A-Fa-f:]*(?:\.[0-9][0-9A-Fa-f:]*)*"
    r"(?:%[\w.%:~+\-]*)?(?![\w:%])(?!\.\d)"
)
_ZONE_RE = re.compile(r"(?:[\w.~\-]|%[0-9A-Fa-f]{2})+")

# These assigned prefixes still fall within ipaddress's broad reserved ranges.
# They can identify translated endpoints / routing segments, not merely code
# resembling an address. IANA IPv6 Special-Purpose Address Registry; RFCs
# 6052, 8215 and 9602. Other reserved-space exclusions remain in effect.
_ASSIGNED_RESERVED = tuple(
    ipaddress.IPv6Network(prefix) for prefix in ("64:ff9b::/96", "64:ff9b:1::/48", "5f00::/16")
)


# A dotted quad labelled as a version ("v2.4.1.0", "version 10.2.14.3",
# "build 1.0.0.7") is not an address, however valid it would be as one. Nor
# is the version in a browser's product token ("Chrome/126.0.0.0") or the last
# field of a Windows package identity ("...~amd64~~6.1.1.3").
_VERSION_LABEL_RE = re.compile(
    r"(?:\bv|\b(?:version|ver\.?|build|release|firmware)\s*[:=]?\s*"
    r"|\b(?:Chrome|Chromium|HeadlessChrome|CriOS|Edg|Edge|EdgA|OPR|Firefox|FxiOS|Safari|Version"
    r"|AppleWebKit|Electron|Trident)/"
    r"|~)$",
    re.IGNORECASE,
)


def _is_nobodys(address: ipaddress.IPv4Address | ipaddress.IPv6Address) -> bool:
    """Whether an address identifies no host: there is nothing to protect in it.

    The unspecified address (``0.0.0.0``, ``::``), loopback (``127.0.0.1``,
    ``::1``), and most reserved space are excluded. This keeps bind addresses
    readable and avoids treating the ``1::2`` of a Python slice or the ``be::``
    of reStructuredText as a host. Assigned translation/routing prefixes are
    exceptions to the reserved-space filter. Mapped addresses follow IPv4's
    classification regardless of their textual representation.
    """
    if isinstance(address, ipaddress.IPv6Address):
        if address.ipv4_mapped is not None:
            return _is_nobodys(address.ipv4_mapped)
        if any(address in network for network in _ASSIGNED_RESERVED):
            return False
    return address.is_unspecified or address.is_loopback or address.is_reserved


class IpDetector:
    name = "ip"

    def find(self, text: str) -> list[Entity]:
        ipv6: list[Entity] = []
        literals: list[Span] = []
        for m in _IPV6_RE.finditer(text):
            candidate = m.group(0).rstrip(".")  # prose punctuation is outside the address
            address, separator, zone = candidate.partition("%")
            if address.count(":") < 2:
                continue
            # Even an invalid IPv6-shaped token must not yield a valid IPv4
            # fragment. Keep its full span when suppressing embedded matches.
            literals.append(Span(m.start(), m.end()))
            if len(address) > 45 or (separator and not _ZONE_RE.fullmatch(zone)):
                continue
            try:
                v6 = ipaddress.IPv6Address(address)
            except ValueError:
                continue
            if v6.is_unspecified or v6.is_loopback:
                continue
            if _is_nobodys(v6):
                # An explicit dotted tail already established an IPv4 identity
                # in the old detector. Protect the enclosing literal, including
                # deprecated IPv4-compatible notation, instead of its tail alone.
                # Low bits 127.0.0.1 do not make a global IPv6 address loopback.
                # Use this fallback only for otherwise excluded reserved space.
                if "." not in address or v6.ipv4_mapped is not None:
                    continue
                if _is_nobodys(ipaddress.IPv4Address(address.rsplit(":", 1)[1])):
                    continue
            ipv6.append(
                Entity(
                    type=EntityType.IPV6,
                    value=candidate,
                    span=Span(m.start(), m.start() + len(candidate)),
                    detector=self.name,
                )
            )
        ipv6_spans = SpanIndex(literals)
        out: list[Entity] = []
        for m in _IPV4_RE.finditer(text):
            if ipv6_spans.overlaps(Span(m.start(), m.end())):
                continue
            try:
                v4 = ipaddress.IPv4Address(m.group(0))
            except ValueError:
                continue
            if _is_nobodys(v4):
                continue
            if _VERSION_LABEL_RE.search(text[max(0, m.start() - 16) : m.start()]):
                continue
            out.append(
                Entity(
                    type=EntityType.IPV4,
                    value=m.group(0),
                    span=Span(m.start(), m.end()),
                    detector=self.name,
                )
            )
        out.extend(ipv6)
        return out
veil/detectors/phone.py:
"""Phone number detector.

Covers exactly two shapes, both structurally strict on purpose:

- NANP (US/Canada): 10 digits as ``area-exchange-line``, ``(area)
  exchange-line``, or ``area.exchange.line``, optionally prefixed with a
  ``1``. Area and exchange codes cannot start with 0 or 1 (real NANP
  numbers never do).
- International: an explicit leading ``+``, a country calling code the ITU
  has assigned, and a national number of a length that country uses, with
  the digits grouped however the writer liked (``+33 1 23 45 67 89``,
  ``+49 30 12345678``, ``+81 3-1234-5678``, ``+44 (0)20 7946 0958``). The
  codes and lengths are in :mod:`veil.detectors._calling_codes`.

There is no third "generic, separator-only, no country code" bucket.
Earlier versions had one (any 7-15 digit run split by spaces/dots/dashes),
and it over-masked: an ISO date (``2026-09-21``), an order number
(``#4417-2291``), or any other dash/dot-separated digit group that isn't
actually NANP- or E.164-shaped would get flagged. Losing that bucket is a
real recall trade-off — some real phone numbers are written without a
country code in a non-NANP format (e.g. a UK number as ``020 7946
0958``) and this detector will miss them — but per-1,000-word false
positives on ordinary business text (``benchmarks/``) matter more here
than that recall gap.

**Context guard.** Even a structurally NANP-shaped 10-digit run can be
something else — an order number, invoice ID, or ticket number that
happens to land on a valid-looking area/exchange code. A candidate
immediately preceded by ``#``, "order", "invoice", "inv-", "ticket", or
"zip" (case-insensitive, within a short window) is dropped.

Structural validation only — there is no offline way to confirm a number
is *assigned*, only that it is *well-formed*.

A dash-separated ``XXX-XX-XXXX`` group is structurally identical to a US
SSN, and a dot-separated group is structurally identical to an IPv4
address (including a *partial* IPv4 octet run). Rather than guess, this
detector defers to :class:`~veil.detectors.ssn.SsnDetector` and
:class:`~veil.detectors.ip.IpDetector`: any phone candidate that overlaps
a span either of them recognizes is dropped.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import re

from veil._spans import DisjointSpans, SpanIndex
from veil.detectors._calling_codes import split_international
from veil.detectors.ip import IpDetector
from veil.detectors.ssn import SsnDetector
from veil.types import Entity, EntityType, Span

_CANDIDATE_RE = re.compile(
    r"(?<![\w])"
    r"(?:"
    r"\+\d{8,15}"  # contiguous, but only with an explicit country-code "+"
    r"|"
    r"(?:\+\d{1,3}[\s.-]?)?(?:\(\d{2,4}\)[\s.-]?)?\d{2,4}(?:[\s.-]\d{2,4}){1,4}"
    r")"
    r"(?![\w])"
)


def _digits(s: str) -> str:
    return re.sub(r"\D", "", s)


_NANP_RE = re.compile(
    r"^\+?1?[\s.-]?\(?(?P<area>[2-9]\d{2})\)?[\s.-]?(?P<exch>[2-9]\d{2})[\s.-]?(?P<line>\d{4})$"
)


def _is_nanp(candidate: str) -> bool:
    return bool(_NANP_RE.match(candidate.strip()))


# "+", then groups of digits. Between two groups: at most one of . - /, with
# an optional space on either side, so "+49 30 / 123456" and "+1 (212)
# 555-1234" hold together and a line break never does.
_GAP = r"(?:[ \u00a0\u202f]?[.\-/]?[ \u00a0\u202f]?)"
_GROUP = r"(?:\(\d{1,5}\)|\d{1,14})"
_INTERNATIONAL_RE = re.compile(rf"(?<![\w+])\+{_GROUP}(?:{_GAP}{_GROUP}){{0,8}}")
_GROUP_RE = re.compile(_GROUP)
# "+32.035815963" is a signed decimal (Go prints its monotonic clock that
# way), and a calendar date ends whatever number came before it.
_SIGNED_DECIMAL_RE = re.compile(r"\+\d+\.\d+")
_ISO_DATE_RE = re.compile(r"(?<!\d)(?:19|20)\d\d-[01]\d-[0-3]\d(?!\d)")
_EXTENSION_RE = re.compile(r"[xX]\d")


def _is_valid_international(digits: str) -> bool:
    parts = split_international(digits)
    if parts is None:
        return False
    code, national = parts
    if code == "1":  # North America: ten digits, area and exchange from 2 up
        return len(national) == 10 and national[0] not in "01" and national[3] not in "01"
    return True


def _international_end(candidate: str) -> int | None:
    """Length of the longest run of leading groups that makes a valid number.

    Digits that follow a number ("+1 212 555 0134 2026") are tried first as
    part of it and then dropped group by group. A "(0)" after the calling
    code is the trunk prefix some countries print for domestic callers; it
    is not part of the number.
    """
    if _SIGNED_DECIMAL_RE.fullmatch(candidate):
        return None
    date = _ISO_DATE_RE.search(candidate)
    if date is not None:
        candidate = candidate[: date.start()]
    groups = list(_GROUP_RE.finditer(candidate))
    for count in range(len(groups), 0, -1):
        digits = "".join(
            _digits(g.group(0))
            for i, g in enumerate(groups[:count])
            if not (i == 1 and g.group(0) == "(0)")
        )
        if 8 <= len(digits) <= 15 and _is_valid_international(digits):
            end = groups[count - 1].end()
            if end == len(candidate) or not candidate[end : end + 1].isdigit():
                return end
    return None


# Order/invoice/ticket/ZIP context that should suppress an otherwise
# NANP-shaped match. "#" alone (a leading number sign right before the
# candidate) is included since it's the single most common order/ticket
# marker ("Order #4417-2291", "Ticket #202-555-0199").
_BLOCKING_CONTEXT_RE = re.compile(r"(#\s*$|\b(order|invoice|inv-|ticket|zip)\b)", re.IGNORECASE)
_CONTEXT_WINDOW = 15


def _has_blocking_context(text: str, start: int) -> bool:
    window = text[max(0, start - _CONTEXT_WINDOW) : start]
    return bool(_BLOCKING_CONTEXT_RE.search(window))


class PhoneDetector:
    name = "phone"

    def __init__(self) -> None:
        self._ip_detector = IpDetector()
        self._ssn_detector = SsnDetector()

    def find(self, text: str) -> list[Entity]:
        ip_spans = [e.span for e in self._ip_detector.find(text)]
        addresses = SpanIndex(ip_spans)
        conflicting = SpanIndex(ip_spans + [e.span for e in self._ssn_detector.find(text)])
        out: list[Entity] = []
        international = DisjointSpans()
        for m in _INTERNATIONAL_RE.finditer(text):
            end = _international_end(m.group(0))
            if end is None:
                continue
            span = Span(m.start(), m.start() + end)
            after = text[span.end : span.end + 2]
            if (after[:1].isalnum() or after[:1] == "_") and not _EXTENSION_RE.match(after):
                continue
            # A calling code and a valid length outweigh the three-two-four
            # shape of a US SSN somewhere inside ("+33 142 78 2350").
            if addresses.overlaps(span) or _has_blocking_context(text, m.start()):
                continue
            international.add(span)
            out.append(
                Entity(
                    type=EntityType.PHONE,
                    value=text[span.start : span.end],
                    span=span,
                    detector=self.name,
                    confidence=0.95,
                )
            )
        for m in _CANDIDATE_RE.finditer(text):
            candidate = m.group(0)
            digits = _digits(candidate)
            if len(digits) < 7:
                continue
            span = Span(m.start(), m.end())
            if conflicting.overlaps(span) or international.overlaps(span):
                continue
            # A "+" form was judged above; only the national shape is left.
            if candidate.startswith("+") or not _is_nanp(candidate):
                continue
            if _has_blocking_context(text, m.start()):
                continue
            out.append(
                Entity(
                    type=EntityType.PHONE,
                    value=candidate,
                    span=span,
                    detector=self.name,
                    confidence=0.95,
                )
            )
        out.sort(key=lambda e: e.span.start)
        return out
veil/detectors/secrets.py:
"""API key and secret token detector.

Recognition uses regex/arithmetic — no network calls, no key
revocation checks:

1. **Known prefixes.** Providers stamp a recognizable prefix on issued
   keys (this is intentional on their part, to make secret scanning
   possible). We match prefix + the provider's typical trailing-character
   length/alphabet.
2. **High-entropy heuristic.** A bare base64-looking token of at least 20
   characters with Shannon entropy above a threshold is flagged at low
   confidence, unless it reads as words. Entropy alone cannot tell a key
   from a file path: ``user/root/rand/_temporary/_task_200811092030`` uses
   as many different characters as a key does. What tells them apart is
   that a path is made of words and a key is not (see
   :mod:`veil.detectors._words`). This still has false positives (ETags,
   lockfile hashes, anything else that really is random) and false
   negatives (short keys) — it's a backstop, not a guarantee.

Explicit Authorization/Proxy-Authorization Basic and Bearer values supply
their own context. Mask each complete token without entropy or word heuristics.
Explicit credential assignments supply context too; short labelled passwords,
API keys, client secrets and OAuth token values become complete secrets.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import math
import re
from bisect import bisect_left
from collections.abc import Iterator

from veil._spans import DisjointSpans, SpanIndex
from veil.detectors._credential_fields import credential_field_spans, is_credential_field
from veil.detectors._http_auth import http_authorization_spans
from veil.detectors._jwt import compact_jwt_spans
from veil.detectors._words import looks_random
from veil.types import Entity, EntityType, Span

# A PEM private key, masked as one block from its BEGIN line to its END line;
# a block cut off before its END line (a truncated paste) runs to the end of
# its base64 body.
_PEM_LABEL = r"((?:[A-Z0-9]+ )*PRIVATE KEY(?: BLOCK)?)"
_PEM_BEGIN_RE = re.compile(rf"-----BEGIN {_PEM_LABEL}-----")
_PEM_END_RE = re.compile(rf"-----END {_PEM_LABEL}-----")
_PEM_BODY_RE = re.compile(r"[A-Za-z0-9+/=:,\s-]*")
_ARMOR_LINE_END_RE = re.compile(r"[ \t]*(?:\r\n|\r|\n)")
_ARMOR_HEADER_RE = re.compile(r"[^:\s]+:[^\r\n]*(?:\r\n|\r|\n|$)")


def _private_key_body_end(text: str, start: int, label: str) -> int:
    pos = start
    if label == "PGP PRIVATE KEY BLOCK" and (line := _ARMOR_LINE_END_RE.match(text, pos)):
        pos = line.end()
        # OpenPGP armor headers precede the base64 body and may contain
        # arbitrary text (especially Comment), not just base64 characters.
        # Skipping their *syntax* retains them inside the opaque secret span.
        while (header := _ARMOR_HEADER_RE.match(text, pos)) is not None:
            pos = header.end()
    body = _PEM_BODY_RE.match(text, pos)
    assert body is not None
    return body.end()


def _private_key_blocks(text: str) -> Iterator[tuple[int, int]]:
    """(start, end) of each PEM private key block, in order.

    The END lines are indexed once. Searching forward for one from every
    BEGIN line rescans the rest of the text for each header that has none.
    """
    closers: dict[str, list[tuple[int, int]]] | None = None
    pos = 0
    while (begin := _PEM_BEGIN_RE.search(text, pos)) is not None:
        if closers is None:
            closers = {}
            for closer in _PEM_END_RE.finditer(text):
                closers.setdefault(closer.group(1), []).append((closer.start(), closer.end()))
        ends = closers.get(begin.group(1), [])
        nxt = bisect_left(ends, (begin.end(),))  # the first END line starting after the header
        if nxt < len(ends):
            pos = ends[nxt][1]
        else:
            pos = _private_key_body_end(text, begin.end(), begin.group(1))
        yield begin.start(), pos


# (name, regex). Known-prefix and compatibility-shape recognition, not
# credential validation. More specific/prefixed formats are matched first so the
# generic, prefix-free `aws_secret_key` pattern (any 40-char alnum run)
# never shadows a more specific match nested inside a longer token.
_KNOWN_PATTERNS: list[tuple[str, re.Pattern[str]]] = [
    # Project/service-account shaped tokens have URL-safe opaque bodies. Do not
    # truncate them at a historical key length or at an internal '-' / '_'.
    # Match the enclosing token before patterns that could recognize a fragment
    # of its body. This is recognition for masking, not credential validation.
    (
        "openai_key",
        re.compile(r"\bsk-(?:proj|svcacct)-[A-Za-z0-9_-]{20,}(?![A-Za-z0-9_-])"),
    ),
    # AWS IAM documents AKIA for long-term and ASIA for STS temporary key IDs.
    # Either known prefix must work without the generic entropy/word heuristic.
    ("aws_access_key", re.compile(r"\b(?:AKIA|ASIA)[0-9A-Z]{16}\b")),
    ("github_pat_classic", re.compile(r"\bghp_[A-Za-z0-9]{36}\b")),
    ("github_pat_fine", re.compile(r"\bgithub_pat_[A-Za-z0-9_]{22,255}\b")),
    ("github_oauth", re.compile(r"\bgho_[A-Za-z0-9]{36}\b")),
    ("slack_token", re.compile(r"\bxox[baprs]-[A-Za-z0-9-]{10,72}\b")),
    ("stripe_live_secret", re.compile(r"\bsk_live_[A-Za-z0-9]{16,99}\b")),
    ("stripe_live_restricted", re.compile(r"\brk_live_[A-Za-z0-9]{16,99}\b")),
    ("anthropic_key", re.compile(r"\bsk-ant-[A-Za-z0-9_-]{20,161}\b")),
    ("openai_key", re.compile(r"\bsk-[A-Za-z0-9]{20,161}\b")),
    ("google_api_key", re.compile(r"\bAIza[0-9A-Za-z_-]{35}\b")),
    ("aws_secret_key", re.compile(r"(?<![A-Za-z0-9/+=])[A-Za-z0-9/+=]{40}(?![A-Za-z0-9/+=])")),
]

_HIGH_ENTROPY_RE = re.compile(r"\b[A-Za-z0-9+/_-]{20,64}\b")
_ENTROPY_THRESHOLD = 4.0


def shannon_entropy(s: str) -> float:
    if not s:
        return 0.0
    counts: dict[str, int] = {}
    for ch in s:
        counts[ch] = counts.get(ch, 0) + 1
    n = len(s)
    return -sum((c / n) * math.log2(c / n) for c in counts.values())


def _entropy_floor(length: int) -> float:
    """The least entropy a token of this length must have to be flagged.

    A token of n characters cannot exceed log2(n) bits per character, so a
    fixed floor of 4.0 passes between an eighth and two thirds of random
    20-character keys, depending on their alphabet, and nearly all of them
    only from 32 characters up. Short tokens are held to four fifths of
    what their length allows instead.
    """
    return min(_ENTROPY_THRESHOLD, 0.8 * math.log2(length))


def _looks_like_id_or_hash(s: str) -> bool:
    # Pure hex (common for hashes/UUID fragments) or a run with no digits at
    # all (likely prose/base64 padding) is not worth flagging at low confidence.
    return bool(re.fullmatch(r"[0-9a-fA-F]+", s)) or not any(ch.isdigit() for ch in s)


class SecretDetector:
    name = "secret"

    def find_in_field(self, name: str, text: str) -> list[Entity]:
        """A supported key identifies its complete decoded string value."""
        if not text or not is_credential_field(name):
            return []
        return [
            Entity(
                type=EntityType.SECRET,
                value=text,
                span=Span(0, len(text)),
                detector=f"{self.name}:credential_field",
                confidence=1.0,
            )
        ]

    def find(self, text: str) -> list[Entity]:
        out: list[Entity] = []
        claimed = DisjointSpans()

        def known(pattern_name: str, start: int, end: int, confidence: float = 0.97) -> None:
            span = Span(start, end)
            if claimed.overlaps(span):
                return
            claimed.add(span)
            out.append(
                Entity(
                    type=EntityType.SECRET,
                    value=text[start:end],
                    span=span,
                    detector=f"{self.name}:{pattern_name}",
                    confidence=confidence,
                )
            )

        fields = [Span(start, end) for start, end in credential_field_spans(text)]
        fields_index = SpanIndex(fields)
        for start, end in _private_key_blocks(text):
            # A field may enclose a whole key, but a label inside an opaque
            # PEM block must never displace the block and expose its body.
            if not fields_index.contains(Span(start, end)):
                # Opaque credentials own nested PII, just as JWTs and explicit
                # auth values do. An email/card match must not displace the
                # enclosing block and leave its otherwise claimed body exposed.
                known("private_key", start, end, confidence=1.0)
        for span in fields:
            known("credential_field", span.start, span.end, confidence=1.0)
        for start, end in http_authorization_spans(text):
            # Context owns the whole credential, including JWT punctuation and
            # padding or a card-shaped fragment that another detector could find.
            known("http_authorization", start, end, confidence=1.0)
        for start, end in compact_jwt_spans(text):
            # A recognized JOSE header identifies the enclosing credential.
            # A card-like signature fragment must not displace its claims.
            known("jwt", start, end, confidence=1.0)
        for pattern_name, rx in _KNOWN_PATTERNS:
            for m in rx.finditer(text):
                # aws_secret_key is the one pattern with no distinguishing
                # prefix (just "40 alnum characters"), so a plain SHA-1 hex
                # hash (also 40 characters) would otherwise false-positive.
                # A 40-character stretch of a file path matches it just as well.
                if pattern_name == "aws_secret_key" and (
                    _looks_like_id_or_hash(m.group(0)) or not looks_random(m.group(0))
                ):
                    continue
                known(pattern_name, m.start(), m.end())

        for m in _HIGH_ENTROPY_RE.finditer(text):
            span = Span(m.start(), m.end())
            if claimed.overlaps(span):
                continue
            candidate = m.group(0)
            if _looks_like_id_or_hash(candidate) or not looks_random(candidate):
                continue
            entropy = shannon_entropy(candidate)
            if entropy < _entropy_floor(len(candidate)):
                continue
            claimed.add(span)
            out.append(
                Entity(
                    type=EntityType.SECRET,
                    value=candidate,
                    span=span,
                    detector=f"{self.name}:high_entropy",
                    confidence=min(0.6, entropy / 8),
                )
            )
        out.sort(key=lambda e: e.span.start)
        return out
veil/detectors/ssn.py:
"""US Social Security Number detector.

Matches ``AAA-GG-SSSS`` (with `-`, ` `, or no separator, used
*consistently* — see below) and excludes area, group, and serial values
the SSA has documented as never issued:

- area ``000``, ``666``, or ``900-999``
- group ``00``
- serial ``0000``

**Consistent-separator requirement.** A US ZIP+4 code (``AAAAA-SSSS``, 5
digits, a dash, 4 digits) is structurally a false positive here: read as
area(3)+group(2)+sep+serial(4), "22156-7224" parses as a well-formed SSN.
Real SSNs are written with a separator at *both* gaps or *neither* —
never one. Requiring the two separators to match rejects the ZIP+4 shape
(no separator before the 2-digit group, one before the last 4) without
needing to special-case "ZIP".

This is a structural check only; it cannot tell whether a well-formed SSN
was ever actually issued to someone.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import re

from veil.types import Entity, EntityType, Span

_SSN_RE = re.compile(
    r"(?<!\d)(?P<area>\d{3})(?P<sep1>[- ]?)(?P<group>\d{2})(?P<sep2>[- ]?)(?P<serial>\d{4})(?!\d)"
)


def is_valid_ssn(area: str, group: str, serial: str) -> bool:
    if area == "000" or area == "666" or area[0] == "9":
        return False
    if group == "00":
        return False
    return serial != "0000"


class SsnDetector:
    name = "ssn"

    def find(self, text: str) -> list[Entity]:
        out: list[Entity] = []
        for m in _SSN_RE.finditer(text):
            if m.group("sep1") != m.group("sep2"):
                continue  # e.g. a ZIP+4 code, not a consistently-formatted SSN
            if not is_valid_ssn(m.group("area"), m.group("group"), m.group("serial")):
                continue
            # Require at least one separator, or explicit "SSN"/"social security"
            # context nearby, to avoid matching arbitrary 9-digit numbers.
            has_sep = "-" in m.group(0) or " " in m.group(0)
            if not has_sep:
                window = text[max(0, m.start() - 25) : m.start()].lower()
                if "ssn" not in window and "social security" not in window:
                    continue
            out.append(
                Entity(
                    type=EntityType.SSN,
                    value=m.group(0),
                    span=Span(m.start(), m.end()),
                    detector=self.name,
                    confidence=0.9 if has_sep else 0.6,
                )
            )
        return out
veil/detectors/url.py:
"""URLs carrying embedded credentials or tokens.

Credential shapes, in a URL of any scheme (``https``, but also connection strings
like ``postgres://``, ``redis://`` or ``mongodb+srv://``, where credentials
are most often embedded):

- Userinfo in the authority: ``scheme://user:password@host/...``.
- A sensitive token in a query or fragment, including percent-encoded names.
- Signed storage/CDN links: AWS/GCS V4, Azure Storage SAS, and the paired
  signature/signer fields of AWS/GCS V2 and CloudFront.

The whole original URL is flagged: credentials are meaningful in context and
rewriting a signed URL can invalidate it. Recognition does not verify a signature.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import re
import string
from collections.abc import Iterator
from urllib.parse import unquote_plus

from veil.types import Entity, EntityType, Span

_SCHEME_START = frozenset(string.ascii_letters)
_SCHEME_CHARS = frozenset(string.ascii_letters + string.digits + "+.-")
_URL_BODY_RE = re.compile(r"[^\s\"'<>]+")
_AUTHORITY_END_RE = re.compile(r"[/\s@]")
_SENSITIVE_NAME = (
    r"(?:api[_-]?key|access[_-]?token|auth[_-]?token|token|secret|password|session[_-]?id)"
)
_SENSITIVE_NAME_RE = re.compile(_SENSITIVE_NAME, re.IGNORECASE)
_SENSITIVE_PARAM_RE = re.compile(r"[?&]" + _SENSITIVE_NAME + r"=[^&\s]+", re.IGNORECASE)


def _sensitive_parameters(component: str) -> bool:
    # Split before decoding, and decode names only once. An encoded '&' or '='
    # inside a value must not invent another parameter. Keep duplicate names
    # with any nonempty value; an empty later duplicate cannot hide a token.
    names = set()
    for field in component.split("&"):
        name, separator, value = field.partition("=")
        if separator and value:
            names.add(unquote_plus(name).lower())
    if any(_SENSITIVE_NAME_RE.fullmatch(name) for name in names):
        return True
    if names & {"x-amz-signature", "x-goog-signature"}:
        return True
    if {"sig", "sv"} <= names:
        return True
    return "signature" in names and bool(
        names & {"googleaccessid", "awsaccesskeyid", "key-pair-id"}
    )


def _has_credential_parameters(url: str) -> bool:
    before_fragment, _, fragment = url.partition("#")
    query = before_fragment.partition("?")[2]
    # OAuth implicit redirects use '#access_token=...'. Client-side routers
    # can use '#/callback?access_token=...'; keep those parameters together,
    # but never combine a query's signer with a fragment's signature.
    return any(
        _sensitive_parameters(component)
        for component in (query, fragment, fragment.partition("?")[2])
        if component
    )


def _is_word(ch: str) -> bool:
    return ch.isalnum() or ch == "_"


def _has_userinfo(url: str) -> bool:
    """Does the authority carry ``user:password@``? The first ``/`` or ``@`` after the
    scheme decides: it must be an ``@``, with a ``:`` and something after it before it."""
    start = url.index("://") + 3
    end = _AUTHORITY_END_RE.search(url, start)
    return end is not None and end.group() == "@" and ":" in url[start : end.start() - 1]


def _urls(text: str) -> Iterator[tuple[int, str]]:
    """Each ``scheme://rest`` in ``text`` as (start, url), leftmost first, without overlap.

    Found from the ``://`` backwards. Matching a scheme forwards from every
    word start rescans a long run of scheme characters (``a.b.c.d...``) once
    per word in it, which takes minutes on a few hundred kilobytes.
    """
    floor = 0  # where the previous URL ended
    search = 0
    while True:
        sep = text.find("://", search)
        if sep == -1:
            return
        search = sep + 3
        run = sep
        while run > floor and text[run - 1] in _SCHEME_CHARS:
            run -= 1
        # The scheme starts at the first letter in the run that begins a word.
        start = next(
            (
                i
                for i in range(run, sep)
                if text[i] in _SCHEME_START and (i == 0 or not _is_word(text[i - 1]))
            ),
            None,
        )
        if start is None:
            continue
        body = _URL_BODY_RE.match(text, sep + 3)
        if body is None:
            continue
        yield start, text[start : body.end()]
        floor = search = body.end()


class UrlCredentialDetector:
    name = "url_credential"

    def find(self, text: str) -> list[Entity]:
        out: list[Entity] = []
        for start, found in _urls(text):
            url = found.rstrip(").,;")
            # Retain legacy raw matches, including router fragments, while
            # adding decoded-name and signing-format recognition.
            if (
                _has_userinfo(url)
                or _SENSITIVE_PARAM_RE.search(url)
                or _has_credential_parameters(url)
            ):
                out.append(
                    Entity(
                        type=EntityType.URL_CREDENTIAL,
                        value=url,
                        span=Span(start, start + len(url)),
                        detector=self.name,
                    )
                )
        return out

Both integrations are optional extras (``veil-pii[anthropic]`` /

veil/integrations/_json_arguments.py:
"""Transform decoded JSON values without rewriting surrounding argument syntax."""

from __future__ import annotations

import json
from dataclasses import dataclass

from veil.masker import Masker
from veil.restore import restore_json_text
from veil.vault import VaultError


def _reject_constant(value: str) -> None:
    raise ValueError("Non-JSON numeric constant")


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class _StringToken:
    start: int
    end: int
    value: str
    is_key: bool


def mask_string_value(value: str, masker: Masker, *, key: str | None = None) -> str:
    """Retain an explicit credential field's context for its string value.

    The prefix is only a detector hint, never a changed key or output field.
    Masker's ordinary request transaction, reservations and exact restoration
    checks still apply to the complete contextual text.
    """
    if key is not None and key.lower() in {"authorization", "proxy-authorization"}:
        prefix = "Authorization: "
        return masker.mask(prefix + value)[len(prefix) :]
    return masker.mask(value, field_name=key)


def _string_tokens(arguments: str) -> list[_StringToken]:
    # Numbers are only validated, never converted to bounded ints or floats.
    json.loads(arguments, parse_int=str, parse_float=str, parse_constant=_reject_constant)
    decoder = json.JSONDecoder()
    tokens: list[_StringToken] = []
    pos = 0
    while (start := arguments.find('"', pos)) != -1:
        value, end = decoder.raw_decode(arguments, start)
        assert isinstance(value, str)
        pos = end
        while pos < len(arguments) and arguments[pos] in " \t\r\n":
            pos += 1
        tokens.append(
            _StringToken(start, end, value, pos < len(arguments) and arguments[pos] == ":")
        )
    return tokens


def _replace_values(arguments: str, tokens: list[_StringToken], replacements: list[str]) -> str:
    pieces: list[str] = []
    pos = 0
    for token, replacement in zip(tokens, replacements, strict=True):
        if replacement != token.value:
            pieces.append(arguments[pos : token.start])
            pieces.append(json.dumps(replacement, ensure_ascii=False))
            pos = token.end
    pieces.append(arguments[pos:])
    return "".join(pieces)


def mask_arguments(arguments: str, masker: Masker) -> str:
    """Mask string values in a complete JSON argument document.

    Scanning the raw document misses entities containing JSON escapes. Re-encoding
    the entire parsed tree, however, changes numeric precision, duplicate members
    and unrelated spelling. Validate first, then replace only changed string tokens.
    Field names cannot safely be renamed; detected sensitive keys reject the request.
    Non-string values retain their types and are outside string-masking coverage.
    """
    try:
        tokens = _string_tokens(arguments)
    except (ValueError, RecursionError):
        raise VaultError("Tool arguments must be complete, valid JSON before masking") from None
    for token in tokens:
        if token.is_key and masker.find_entities(token.value):
            raise VaultError(
                "Tool arguments contain a sensitive JSON key; use a non-sensitive field name"
            )
    values: list[tuple[_StringToken, str | None]] = []
    for index, token in enumerate(tokens):
        if token.is_key:
            continue
        previous = tokens[index - 1] if index else None
        # A key supplies context only to its immediate string value. Arrays
        # and nested objects must not inherit a header name from an ancestor.
        key = (
            previous.value
            if previous is not None
            and previous.is_key
            and arguments[previous.end : token.start].strip() == ":"
            else None
        )
        values.append((token, key))
    # Reserve all decoded literal text together, including escaped placeholder
    # examples, so one value cannot acquire another value's existing literal token.
    with masker._masking_batch() as batch:
        for token, _ in values:
            batch.reserve(token.value)
        masked = [mask_string_value(token.value, masker, key=key) for token, key in values]
    return _replace_values(arguments, [token for token, _ in values], masked)


def restore_arguments(arguments: str, masker: Masker) -> str:
    """Restore complete string values without coercing unrelated tool data.

    Complete values retain tolerant restoration. For malformed or truncated model
    output, the streaming lexer still makes its existing best effort without
    inventing syntax. Neither path renames keys or converts numeric tokens.
    """
    try:
        values = [token for token in _string_tokens(arguments) if not token.is_key]
    except (ValueError, RecursionError):
        return restore_json_text(arguments, masker.vault)
    return _replace_values(arguments, values, [masker.restore(token.value) for token in values])

"""The masking pipeline: text -> (masked text, vault).

Ties together detectors, name backends, a surrogate generator, and a vault.
Detector results are pooled, overlaps resolved (higher confidence wins,
ties broken by longer span, then earliest detector), and replaced in
reading order, so the first value of a type in a text is numbered 1.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

from collections.abc import Iterator, Sequence
from contextlib import contextmanager
from dataclasses import dataclass, field

from veil._spans import DisjointSpans
from veil.backends.base import NameBackend
from veil.detectors import default_detectors
from veil.detectors.base import Detector, FieldDetector
from veil.restore import restore_exact, restore_tolerant
from veil.surrogates import PlaceholderSurrogates, SurrogateGenerator
from veil.types import Entity
from veil.vault import Vault, VaultError


def _spelling(text: str) -> str:
    # Conservative reservation for the case/whitespace rewrites accepted by
    # tolerant restoration. The final check uses the actual restorers as well.
    return " ".join(text.split()).casefold()


@dataclass
class _MaskingBatch:
    sources: dict[str, list[str]] = field(default_factory=dict)
    pairs: list[tuple[str, str]] = field(default_factory=list)
    used: set[str] = field(default_factory=set)
    originals: set[str] = field(default_factory=set)

    def reserve(self, text: str) -> None:
        normalized = _spelling(text)
        # Index once per source, not once per candidate surrogate. The usual
        # placeholder delimiter is absent from most texts in a large batch.
        # Add later nested inputs too: the final check must see every source.
        for char in set(normalized):
            self.sources.setdefault(char, []).append(normalized)

    def available(self, surrogate: str) -> bool:
        normalized = _spelling(surrogate)
        return (
            bool(normalized)
            and normalized not in self.originals
            and not any(normalized in source for source in self.sources.get(normalized[0], ()))
        )


def _resolve_overlaps(entities: list[Entity]) -> list[Entity]:
    """Greedily keep non-overlapping entities, preferring higher confidence
    then longer span then earlier start, matching how a careful reviewer
    would break ties by hand.
    """
    ranked = sorted(
        entities,
        key=lambda e: (-e.confidence, -len(e.span), e.span.start),
    )
    kept: list[Entity] = []
    taken = DisjointSpans()
    for entity in ranked:
        if taken.overlaps(entity.span):
            continue
        taken.add(entity.span)
        kept.append(entity)
    kept.sort(key=lambda e: e.span.start)
    return kept


@dataclass
class Masker:
    """Reuse a vault so repeated values keep the same surrogate. Use
    :meth:`mask_many` for related raw texts: reservations cover the whole
    batch, including literal examples in other messages. Source texts are
    not retained between batches; include earlier raw texts when adding turns.
    """

    detectors: list[Detector] = field(default_factory=default_detectors)
    name_backends: list[NameBackend] = field(default_factory=list)
    surrogate_generator: SurrogateGenerator = field(default_factory=PlaceholderSurrogates)
    vault: Vault = field(default_factory=Vault)
    _batch: _MaskingBatch | None = field(default=None, init=False, repr=False, compare=False)

    @contextmanager
    def _masking_batch(self) -> Iterator[_MaskingBatch]:
        """Internal request boundary. No prepared output may escape before exit.

        Wrappers nest their ordinary mask calls here, before invoking the SDK.
        A batch retains source text only until preparation finishes. Maskers
        and their vaults are for sequential use, not shared concurrent writes.
        """
        if self._batch is not None:
            yield self._batch
            return
        batch = _MaskingBatch(originals={_spelling(s) for s in self.vault.originals()})
        with self.vault._transaction():
            self._batch = batch
            try:
                yield batch
                if any(not batch.available(s) for s in batch.used):
                    raise VaultError(
                        "a surrogate conflicts with another input in this request; "
                        "remask the complete input with a fresh vault using mask_many"
                    )
                for source, masked in batch.pairs:
                    if (
                        restore_exact(masked, self.vault) != source
                        or restore_tolerant(masked, self.vault) != source
                    ):
                        raise VaultError(
                            "source text would change during surrogate restoration; "
                            "use a fresh vault to remask the complete input"
                        )
            finally:
                self._batch = None

    def mask_many(self, texts: Sequence[str]) -> list[str]:
        """Mask related raw texts together, reserving literals across all of them.

        Either every result restores to its source or VaultError is raised and
        this batch's vault changes are undone. No earlier source texts are kept
        between calls; submit the complete raw conversation when adding turns.
        """
        if isinstance(texts, str):
            raise TypeError("mask_many expects a sequence of strings, not one string")
        with self._masking_batch() as batch:
            for text in texts:
                batch.reserve(text)
            return [self._mask(text, batch) for text in texts]

    def find_entities(self, text: str, *, field_name: str | None = None) -> list[Entity]:
        """Resolve text candidates, optionally retaining its immediate field name.

        Only detectors implementing FieldDetector interpret the hint. The name
        does not become part of the text or propagate to nested values.
        """
        found: list[Entity] = []
        if field_name is not None:
            for detector in self.detectors:
                if isinstance(detector, FieldDetector):
                    found.extend(detector.find_in_field(field_name, text))
        for detector in self.detectors:
            found.extend(detector.find(text))
        for backend in self.name_backends:
            found.extend(backend.find(text))
        return _resolve_overlaps(found)

    def mask(self, text: str, *, field_name: str | None = None) -> str:
        """Mask one text, optionally retaining its immediate string field's name.

        ``field_name`` lets supporting detectors recognize a short credential
        without inventing a serialized prefix. It does not mask the key itself.
        Ambiguous restoration rejects without changing the vault.
        """
        if field_name is None:
            return self.mask_many([text])[0]
        with self._masking_batch() as batch:
            batch.reserve(text)
            return self._mask(text, batch, field_name=field_name)

    def _mask(self, text: str, batch: _MaskingBatch, *, field_name: str | None = None) -> str:
        parts: list[str] = []
        pos = 0
        for entity in self.find_entities(text, field_name=field_name):
            batch.originals.add(_spelling(entity.value))
            surrogate = self.vault.get_or_create(
                entity.type,
                entity.value,
                self.surrogate_generator,
                entity.detector,
                available=batch.available,
            )
            batch.used.add(surrogate)
            parts.append(text[pos : entity.span.start])
            parts.append(surrogate)
            pos = entity.span.end
        parts.append(text[pos:])
        masked = "".join(parts)
        batch.pairs.append((text, masked))
        return masked

    def restore(self, text: str, *, tolerant: bool = True) -> str:
        """Restore surrogates in ``text`` using this masker's vault.

        ``tolerant=True`` (the default) also catches case changes and
        possessives a model commonly introduces; pass ``False`` for
        byte-exact matching only. For a token stream, use
        :class:`veil.restore.Restorer` directly instead.
        """
        return restore_tolerant(text, self.vault) if tolerant else restore_exact(text, self.vault)
veil/restore.py:
"""Restoring surrogates back to their original values.

Three entry points:

- :func:`restore_exact` — surrogate substrings must match byte-for-byte.
  A model that alters a
  surrogate (recapitalizes a fake name, adds a possessive) won't be
  caught.
- :func:`restore_tolerant` — additionally catches the rewrites models
  actually make in practice: case changes, a trailing possessive
  (``Avery Alder's`` -> ``<original>'s``), and a surrogate split across a
  line wrap. It is intentionally conservative (a rewritten surrogate
  must stand as a word of its own) because a
  looser tolerant match risks restoring text that was never a surrogate
  in the first place — the exact opposite of what a privacy tool should
  do. It is **not** applied inside a streaming session; streaming uses
  exact matching only (see :class:`Restorer`) since case/possessive
  rewrites cannot be verified until the trailing context has arrived.
- :class:`Restorer` — the streaming version of :func:`restore_exact`,
  built on a trie so it can emit text as soon as it is provably not part
  of any surrogate, holding back only the shortest possible-prefix
  suffix.

**Streaming, concretely.** If the vault maps ``⟨EMAIL_1⟩`` to
``alice@example.com`` and the model streams the tokens ``"...⟨EM"``,
``"AIL_1⟩ sent it"``, a naive restorer that scans each chunk in isolation
would emit ``⟨EM`` verbatim (leaking the placeholder) and then fail to
recognize ``AIL_1⟩`` as the tail of a surrogate it already partially saw.
:class:`Restorer` instead holds ``⟨EM`` back after the first chunk (it is
a valid prefix of a known surrogate) and only emits once the second chunk
completes or definitively rules out the match.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import json
from dataclasses import dataclass, field

from veil.vault import Vault


def restore_exact(text: str, vault: Vault) -> str:
    """Replace every exact surrogate occurrence with its original value."""
    r = Restorer(vault)
    return r.feed(text) + r.flush()


def restore_json_text(text: str, vault: Vault) -> str:
    """:func:`restore_exact` for serialized JSON: see ``Restorer(json_string=True)``."""
    r = Restorer(vault, json_string=True)
    return r.feed(text) + r.flush()


def restore_tolerant(text: str, vault: Vault) -> str:
    """:func:`restore_exact`, plus the rewrites models make to a surrogate:
    case changes, a trailing possessive, and a surrogate split across
    whitespace or a line break (e.g. a name wrapped mid-token by the model's
    own line width). A rewritten surrogate has to stand as a word of its own
    to count (``avery alderman`` is left alone); an exact one is restored
    wherever it appears.

    One pass over ``text``: a restored value is never scanned again, so an
    original that happens to read like another value's surrogate stays as it
    is.
    """
    exact = _trie(vault)
    loose = _loose_trie(vault)
    out: list[str] = []
    pos = 0
    n = len(text)
    while pos < n:
        ch = text[pos]
        hit = _longest_exact(exact, text, pos) if ch in exact.children else None
        if hit is None and ch.casefold() in loose.children and not _mid_word(text, pos):
            hit = _longest_loose(loose, text, pos)
        if hit is None:
            out.append(ch)
            pos += 1
        else:
            pos, original = hit
            out.append(original)
    return "".join(out)


def _is_word(ch: str) -> bool:
    return ch.isalnum() or ch == "_"


def _mid_word(text: str, pos: int) -> bool:
    """Would a match starting or ending at ``pos`` cut a word in two? ``avery alderman``
    is not ``Avery Alder``; a bracketed placeholder is delimited whatever it touches."""
    return 0 < pos < len(text) and _is_word(text[pos - 1]) and _is_word(text[pos])


@dataclass
class _TrieNode:
    children: dict[str, _TrieNode] = field(default_factory=dict)
    terminal: str | None = None  # original value, if a surrogate ends here
    ambiguous: bool = False  # conflicting originals share a tolerant spelling


def _json_escaped(value: str, *, ascii_only: bool) -> str:
    """``value`` as it appears between the quotes of a JSON string literal."""
    return json.dumps(value, ensure_ascii=ascii_only)[1:-1]


def _build_trie(vault: Vault) -> _TrieNode:
    root = _TrieNode()

    def add(surrogate: str, original: str) -> None:
        node = root
        for ch in surrogate:
            node = node.children.setdefault(ch, _TrieNode())
        node.terminal = original

    for mapping in vault.mappings():
        add(mapping.surrogate, mapping.original)
    return root


def _trie(vault: Vault) -> _TrieNode:
    """The vault's surrogate trie, built once per vault state rather than per string restored."""
    key = "trie"
    trie = vault._derived.get(key)
    if trie is None:
        trie = vault._derived[key] = _build_trie(vault)
    return trie


def _loose_trie(vault: Vault) -> _TrieNode:
    """Surrogates as :func:`restore_tolerant` matches them: case-folded, with the
    spaces between a surrogate's words standing for any run of whitespace."""
    trie = vault._derived.get("loose_trie")
    if trie is None:
        trie = _TrieNode()
        for surrogate in vault.surrogates():
            mapping = vault.lookup_surrogate(surrogate)
            words = [w for w in surrogate.split(" ") if w]
            if mapping is None or not words:
                continue
            node = trie
            for ch in " ".join(words).casefold():
                node = node.children.setdefault(ch, _TrieNode())
            if node.terminal is not None and node.terminal != mapping.original:
                node.ambiguous = True
                node.terminal = None
            elif not node.ambiguous:
                node.terminal = mapping.original
        vault._derived["loose_trie"] = trie
    return trie


def _longest_exact(trie: _TrieNode, text: str, pos: int) -> tuple[int, str] | None:
    """The longest surrogate starting at ``pos``, as (end, original)."""
    node = trie
    best: tuple[int, str] | None = None
    for i in range(pos, len(text)):
        nxt = node.children.get(text[i])
        if nxt is None:
            break
        node = nxt
        if node.terminal is not None:
            best = (i + 1, node.terminal)
    return best


def _longest_loose(trie: _TrieNode, text: str, pos: int) -> tuple[int, str] | None:
    """The longest rewritten surrogate starting at ``pos`` and ending at a word boundary."""
    node = trie
    best: tuple[int, str] | None = None
    i = pos
    n = len(text)
    while i < n:
        ch = text[i]
        gap = node.children.get(" ") if ch.isspace() else None
        if gap is not None:
            while i < n and text[i].isspace():
                i += 1
            node = gap
            continue
        matched = True
        for folded in ch.casefold():
            nxt = node.children.get(folded)
            if nxt is None:
                matched = False
                break
            node = nxt
        if not matched:
            break
        i += 1
        if node.terminal is not None and not _mid_word(text, i):
            best = (i, node.terminal)
    return best


class Restorer:
    """Streaming, exact-match surrogate restorer.

    Call :meth:`feed` with each chunk as it arrives and concatenate the
    returned strings; call :meth:`flush` once at the end of the stream to
    get any text still held back. ``"".join(restorer.feed(c) for c in
    chunks) + restorer.flush()`` is guaranteed equal to
    ``restore_exact("".join(chunks), vault)`` regardless of how the text
    was split into chunks — this is what the Hypothesis property tests in
    ``tests/test_restore_streaming.py`` check.

    With ``json_string=True`` feed serialized JSON from its beginning, such as
    a tool call's streamed arguments. String values are decoded for matching
    (including mixed Unicode escapes); originals are written JSON-escaped.
    Object keys, numbers and structural syntax are unchanged. Untouched text
    keeps its exact spelling. This is a streaming transformer, not a validator
    or a repair tool for malformed JSON.
    """

    def __init__(self, vault: Vault, *, json_string: bool = False) -> None:
        self._trie = _trie(vault)
        self._buffer = ""
        self._json = _JSONRestorer(self._trie) if json_string else None

    def feed(self, chunk: str) -> str:
        if self._json is not None:
            return self._json.feed(chunk)
        self._buffer += chunk
        emitted, self._buffer = self._consume(self._buffer, final=False)
        return emitted

    def flush(self) -> str:
        if self._json is not None:
            return self._json.feed("", final=True)
        emitted, remainder = self._consume(self._buffer, final=True)
        self._buffer = ""
        assert remainder == ""  # a final pass never holds anything back
        return emitted

    def _consume(self, buffer: str, *, final: bool) -> tuple[str, str]:
        out: list[str] = []
        pos = 0
        n = len(buffer)
        while pos < n:
            node = self._trie
            i = pos
            best_end: int | None = None
            best_original: str | None = None
            broke = False
            while i < n:
                nxt = node.children.get(buffer[i])
                if nxt is None:
                    broke = True
                    break
                node = nxt
                i += 1
                if node.terminal is not None:
                    best_end = i
                    best_original = node.terminal
            if not final and not broke and i == n and node.children:
                # Ran out of buffer mid-prefix; more input could still
                # complete a (possibly longer) surrogate. Hold this tail.
                break
            if best_end is not None:
                out.append(best_original or "")
                pos = best_end
                continue
            # No surrogate can start at `pos` no matter what follows.
            out.append(buffer[pos])
            pos += 1
        return "".join(out), buffer[pos:]


_ESCAPES = {'"': '"', "\\": "\\", "/": "/", "b": "\b", "f": "\f", "n": "\n", "r": "\r", "t": "\t"}
_HEX = frozenset("0123456789abcdefABCDEF")


def _json_unit(text: str, pos: int, *, final: bool) -> tuple[str, int] | None:
    """One decoded code point and its raw end, or an incomplete escape.

    Retaining the raw spelling separately is essential: a literal backslash
    followed by ``u27e8`` must never turn into a placeholder delimiter.
    """
    if text[pos] != "\\":
        return text[pos], pos + 1
    if pos + 1 == len(text):
        return ("\\", pos + 1) if final else None
    escape = text[pos + 1]
    if escape in _ESCAPES:
        return _ESCAPES[escape], pos + 2
    if escape != "u":
        return text[pos : pos + 2], pos + 2  # invalid: preserve, never repair
    end = pos + 6
    if end > len(text):
        return (text[pos:], len(text)) if final else None
    digits = text[pos + 2 : end]
    if not all(ch in _HEX for ch in digits):
        return text[pos:end], end
    code = int(digits, 16)
    if 0xD800 <= code <= 0xDBFF:
        if end + 6 > len(text) and not final:
            return None
        low_digits = text[end + 2 : end + 6]
        if (
            text[end : end + 2] == "\\u"
            and len(low_digits) == 4
            and all(ch in _HEX for ch in low_digits)
        ):
            low = int(low_digits, 16)
            if 0xDC00 <= low <= 0xDFFF:
                return chr(0x10000 + (code - 0xD800) * 0x400 + low - 0xDC00), end + 6
    return chr(code), end


class _JSONRestorer:
    """Decode only string values; retain raw units until a trie match is known.

    Retained text is bounded by the longest surrogate prefix plus an incomplete
    escape (at most 11 characters). Container state uses one flag per nesting
    level. An entire tool-call string is never buffered just to parse its JSON.
    """

    def __init__(self, trie: _TrieNode) -> None:
        self._trie = trie
        self._tail = ""
        self._units: list[tuple[str, str]] = []
        self._inside = False
        self._restore_string = False
        self._objects: list[bool] = []
        self._key_expected = False

    def _release(self, *, final: bool) -> str:
        out: list[str] = []
        pos = 0
        while pos < len(self._units):
            node = self._trie
            cursor = pos
            best: tuple[int, str] | None = None
            while cursor < len(self._units):
                nxt = node.children.get(self._units[cursor][0])
                if nxt is None:
                    break
                node = nxt
                cursor += 1
                if node.terminal is not None:
                    best = cursor, node.terminal
            else:
                if not final and node.children:
                    break
            if best is not None:
                pos, original = best
                out.append(_json_escaped(original, ascii_only=False))
            else:
                out.append(self._units[pos][1])
                pos += 1
        del self._units[:pos]
        return "".join(out)

    def feed(self, chunk: str, *, final: bool = False) -> str:
        text = self._tail + chunk
        self._tail = ""
        out: list[str] = []
        pos = 0
        while pos < len(text):
            ch = text[pos]
            if self._inside:
                if ch == '"':
                    out.append(self._release(final=True))
                    out.append(ch)
                    self._inside = False
                    pos += 1
                    continue
                unit = _json_unit(text, pos, final=final)
                if unit is None:
                    self._tail = text[pos:]
                    break
                decoded, end = unit
                raw = text[pos:end]
                if self._restore_string:
                    self._units.append((decoded, raw))
                else:
                    out.append(raw)
                pos = end
                continue
            if ch == '"':
                self._inside = True
                self._restore_string = not self._key_expected
            elif ch in "{[":
                self._objects.append(ch == "{")
                self._key_expected = ch == "{"
            elif ch in "}]":
                if self._objects:
                    self._objects.pop()
                self._key_expected = False
            elif ch == ":":
                self._key_expected = False
            elif ch == ",":
                self._key_expected = bool(self._objects and self._objects[-1])
            out.append(ch)
            pos += 1
        out.append(self._release(final=final))
        return "".join(out)
veil/surrogates.py:
"""Surrogate generation: turning a detected value into a stand-in for the LLM.

Two styles, both documented with their trade-off:

- :class:`PlaceholderSurrogates` emits tokens like ``⟨PERSON_1⟩``. This is
  the robust default: the model cannot mistake a placeholder for a real
  value, and restoration only has to find the exact token back. The
  trade-off is that placeholders visibly interrupt the model's prose ("Dear
  ⟨PERSON_1⟩, your order ⟨CARD_1⟩ ...") which can make responses read
  stiffly and, in rare cases, confuses a model into commenting on the
  bracket syntax itself.
- :class:`RealisticSurrogates` emits fakes that are the right *shape*
  (a plausible name, an `example.com` email, a 555-0100-range phone
  number, a Luhn-valid test card) so the model's prose stays natural and
  it can do arithmetic/formatting on the value as if it were real. The
  trade-off is weaker guarantees: a fake can coincidentally collide with
  something the model says on its own, format-preserving fakes leak
  *structure* (e.g. a fake IBAN still reveals the real one's country), and
  a careless restore step could mistake an incidental example.com address
  the model invented for a surrogate.

Both generators are consistent within a :class:`~veil.vault.Vault`: the
vault, not the generator, is what remembers "this original already has a
surrogate" (see :meth:`veil.vault.Vault.get_or_create`). The generator's
job is only to mint a *new* surrogate the first time a value is seen.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

from dataclasses import dataclass
from typing import Protocol, runtime_checkable

from veil.detectors.card import luhn_ok
from veil.types import EntityType

_FIRST_NAMES = (
    "Avery", "Blair", "Casey", "Dana", "Ellis", "Frankie", "Greer", "Harper",
    "Iris", "Jules", "Kai", "Lane", "Morgan", "Noor", "Oakley", "Parker",
    "Quinn", "Reese", "Sage", "Tatum", "Uma", "Val", "Wren", "Yuki",
)  # fmt: skip
_LAST_NAMES = (
    "Alder", "Brooks", "Castillo", "Delgado", "Ellison", "Farrow", "Grant",
    "Haas", "Ibarra", "Jansen", "Kwan", "Lindqvist", "Moreau", "Nakamura",
    "Okafor", "Petrov", "Quaye", "Rousseau", "Salazar", "Tanaka", "Ueda",
    "Vance", "Wu", "Yilmaz",

_ORG_WORDS = (

    "Gantry", "Hearth", "Ironwood", "Juniper", "Kestrel", "Lattice",
)  # fmt: skip
_ORG_SUFFIXES = ("Inc.", "LLC", "Co.", "Group", "Partners", "Labs")

# RFC 2606 reserved for documentation/examples; will never resolve to a
# real mailbox that receives mail.
_EXAMPLE_DOMAINS = ("example.com", "example.org", "example.net")

# NANP reserves area-code-555-01XX (100 numbers per area code) for fiction
# (see NANPA / ATIS guidelines commonly cited as "555-0100 through
# 555-0199"). We cycle through a handful of plausible US area codes.
_FAKE_AREA_CODES = ("202", "212", "312", "415", "512", "617", "702", "917")

# Published test card prefixes that are documented as never issued to real
# cardholders (Visa/Mastercard/Amex test-number ranges used by payment
# processors' own sandboxes). We generate the trailing digits and append a
# real Luhn check digit so `luhn_ok()` on the output is always true.
_FAKE_CARD_PREFIXES = {
    "visa": "400000",
    "mastercard": "510000",
    "amex": "370000",
}


def _luhn_check_digit(partial: str) -> str:
    # Append a placeholder, compute what check digit makes it valid.
    for digit in "0123456789":
        if luhn_ok(partial + digit):
            return digit
    raise AssertionError("unreachable: a Luhn check digit always exists")  # pragma: no cover


def fake_card_number(index: int, brand: str = "visa") -> str:
    prefix = _FAKE_CARD_PREFIXES[brand]
    body_len = (15 if brand == "amex" else 16) - len(prefix) - 1
    body = str(index % (10**body_len)).zfill(body_len)
    partial = prefix + body
    return partial + _luhn_check_digit(partial)


@runtime_checkable
class SurrogateGenerator(Protocol):
    """Mints a fresh surrogate for a first-seen value of a given type."""

    def generate(self, entity_type: EntityType, original: str, index: int) -> str: ...


@dataclass
class PlaceholderSurrogates:
    """``⟨TYPE_N⟩``-style tokens. ``template`` takes ``{type}`` and ``{n}``."""

    template: str = "⟨{type}_{n}⟩"

    def generate(self, entity_type: EntityType, original: str, index: int) -> str:
        return self.template.format(type=entity_type.value, n=index)


@dataclass
class RealisticSurrogates:
    """Format-preserving fakes; falls back to a placeholder for types with
    no realistic generator defined (SSN, IBAN, IP, secrets, DOB, address,
    URL-credential) since a "realistic" fake there is either meaningless
    (an IP has no fictional-reserved block for this purpose) or actively
    unsafe (a fake secret that *looks* like a real key format).
    """

    fallback: PlaceholderSurrogates = None  # type: ignore[assignment]

    def __post_init__(self) -> None:
        if self.fallback is None:
            self.fallback = PlaceholderSurrogates()

    def generate(self, entity_type: EntityType, original: str, index: int) -> str:
        # These pools are finite. Cycling after exhaustion made Vault retry
        # forever; a numbered placeholder preserves uniqueness and reversibility.
        capacity = {
            EntityType.PERSON: len(_FIRST_NAMES) * len(_LAST_NAMES),
            EntityType.ORG: len(_ORG_WORDS) * len(_ORG_SUFFIXES),
            EntityType.PHONE: len(_FAKE_AREA_CODES) * 100,
        }.get(entity_type)
        if capacity is not None and index > capacity:
            return self.fallback.generate(entity_type, original, index)
        if entity_type is EntityType.PERSON:
            first = _FIRST_NAMES[index % len(_FIRST_NAMES)]
            last = _LAST_NAMES[(index // len(_FIRST_NAMES)) % len(_LAST_NAMES)]
            return f"{first} {last}"
        if entity_type is EntityType.ORG:
            word = _ORG_WORDS[index % len(_ORG_WORDS)]
            suffix = _ORG_SUFFIXES[(index // len(_ORG_WORDS)) % len(_ORG_SUFFIXES)]
            return f"{word} {suffix}"
        if entity_type is EntityType.EMAIL:
            local = f"user{index}"
            domain = _EXAMPLE_DOMAINS[index % len(_EXAMPLE_DOMAINS)]
            return f"{local}@{domain}"
        if entity_type is EntityType.PHONE:
            area = _FAKE_AREA_CODES[(index // 100) % len(_FAKE_AREA_CODES)]
            # NANP reserves 555-0100..555-0199 in every area code for
            # fiction (film/TV, docs, tests); cycle through it.
            line = index % 100
            return f"{area}-555-01{line:02d}"
        if entity_type is EntityType.CARD:
            brands = ("visa", "mastercard", "amex")
            return fake_card_number(index, brands[index % len(brands)])
        return self.fallback.generate(entity_type, original, index)

"""Shared data types used across detectors, surrogates, and the vault.

Kept dependency-free and immutable where practical so that the core package
has zero runtime dependencies and is safe to pass across threads.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

from dataclasses import dataclass, field
from enum import Enum


class EntityType(str, Enum):
    """Categories of sensitive value veil knows how to detect or accept.

    String-valued so surrogate tokens (e.g. ``EMAIL_1``) can be built
    directly from ``.value`` and so the vault serializes as plain JSON.
    """

    EMAIL = "EMAIL"
    PHONE = "PHONE"
    CARD = "CARD"
    IBAN = "IBAN"
    SSN = "SSN"
    IPV4 = "IPV4"
    IPV6 = "IPV6"
    URL_CREDENTIAL = "URL_CREDENTIAL"
    SECRET = "SECRET"
    DOB = "DOB"
    ADDRESS = "ADDRESS"
    PERSON = "PERSON"
    ORG = "ORG"
    LOCATION = "LOCATION"

    def __str__(self) -> str:  # pragma: no cover - trivial
        return self.value


@dataclass(frozen=True, slots=True)
class Span:
    """A half-open character range ``[start, end)`` in some source text."""

    start: int
    end: int

    def __post_init__(self) -> None:
        if self.start < 0 or self.end < self.start:
            raise ValueError(f"invalid span: start={self.start} end={self.end}")

    def __len__(self) -> int:
        return self.end - self.start

    def overlaps(self, other: Span) -> bool:
        return self.start < other.end and other.start < self.end


@dataclass(frozen=True, slots=True)
class Entity:
    """One detected (or supplied) sensitive value, located in source text."""

    type: EntityType
    value: str
    span: Span
    detector: str
    confidence: float = 1.0

    def __post_init__(self) -> None:
        if not 0.0 <= self.confidence <= 1.0:
            raise ValueError(f"confidence must be in [0, 1], got {self.confidence}")


@dataclass(frozen=True, slots=True)
class Mapping:
    """One entry in the vault: an original value bound to its surrogate."""

    type: EntityType
    original: str
    surrogate: str
    first_seen: str = field(default="")  # detector name, for provenance/debugging
